COVID: Second Wave KZN [5840]

By: Carol Albertyn Christie | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Further information:
KZN has become the epicentre of the COVID crisis at the moment.
People are unable to get the medical attention that they need. Ambulances are turned away from hopsitals. The system just cannot cope.

In early December it was projected that the surge would move from the Eastern and Western Cape to Kwa-Zulu Natal.
At the beginning of December we saw a spike in cases because matrics attended RAGE. Over 1000 young aduls were affected and they took that back to where they originally came from.
KZN then had the influx of holiday makers to our shores.
With the added complication of mask fatigue it was just a powder keg waiting to explode.
Yesterday Umhlanga hospital ran out of oxygen.

It is not the fault of the hopsitals that they cannot cope. It is a problem worlwide of countries not being able to cope with the volume of patients.

Lack of staff over stretched personel sub optimal health care.
8723 health care workers infected with COVID since beginning of the pandemic. 98 have died (1%) and 56% of those were nurses.
Video footage of guard of honour
Umhlanga hospital 18 deaths in past two days.
Second wave worse than first.
Prince Msheiyeni Hospital in Umlazi CEO told families that mortuary has reached its capacity.
Some state hospitals like Prince Mshiyeni not able to sparate COVID with non COVID.
Shortage of coffins. Mluleki Madlala of Madlala Funeral Services. He says body count triple as opposed to other Decembers.
Increase of aout 10 bodies a day at crematorium. Extend burning till 11pm at night.


Dr Richard Lessells of KRISP will talk about the new variant, how it developed and what the new charactersics are. It seems that it is more contagious and affects a wider range of people.

Prof Karim will grant us an interview on Monday. (Before he sees the BBC)

Dr Alex Signal works at the Africal Health Research Insititute and he has been testing the difference between the two variuants. Apparently they are on the brink of some new information about the virus which they will release in a week. I am hoping we can break this on Carte Blanche I will be seaking to him this morning.

Michelle heads up a private Ambulance service called Meditech and they are allowing a cameraman to go with them on their rounds. She talks very clearly about patients being turned away.

Dr Kevi Naidu is a gem and he has a practise in Berea. He looks after the Salvation Army Old Age home across the way from him. There are 50 people in the old age home. 26 have covid and two have died. They cannot get to hopsital because of their age and they rely on donations from people for medicine. They have all been quarentined in their little rooms and there is nothing they can do but see how the virus plays out . It is a real waiting game. We cannot interview any of them but there is some footage on Facebook and we can talk to their leader in Johannesburg.

Dr Ashraf Moosa is part of a private hospital consortium and will give the perspective of the hopsitals. He is on various medical boards and speak very authoratively on what is happening.

Patients.

Anele Mzobe lives in Eastern Cape, went home for holidays, knew people had attended a funeral many were infected and died because it is just too far to get to a hospital. He lives in a settlement called Frasier and works in Ballito. He says he has seen many people dying there too.

Owen Govender, son of Vanessa Govender who died working on COVID wards. RK Khan Hopsital. Gave her a guard of honour. Left a message for journalist to get their contact numbers.
0740657007









Valeria Jordan

Graham on oxygen machine , got pneumonia. 61 turns on 23rd.

Go to hospital get medical attention. Just continue panado.
23rd of December on birthday, fevers, Christmas better and not great.
Fevers never broke, Valerie got sick on 26th, Monday got tests Tues, none get better get worse.
Westville hopsital say,
Admitted us lay in tent, put onto drips, afternoon blood results high and had pneumonia, very hot, did not know what happened. Found beds in Harrismith. Graham sent Harrismith, 5 or 6 to Harrismith.
Tues 1st of January. In hospital since 29th.

Ambulance in hot car.

Relieved go home, couldn’t treat him at home.

Stubborn person.

It’s been horrible. Hasn’t heard from him. Can’t speak because of oxygen.
Send he is OK.
Staff is hectic, very full, limited insulin, running haggard.

Second Wave Script 5


Link
It’s been a hell of a year, South Africa recorded it’s first COVID 19 case on the 5th of March 2019 , since then we have had well over a million cases, tens of thousands of deaths and the new variant is driving an aggressive second wave.

(Worldometers.info COVID Cases 1 246 643, Deaths 33 579)

V/O
It dominated KwaZulu-Natal in December and it’s now well on it’s way to Gauteng.

At the peak of the first COVID wave in August last year the active infection rate reached over 44 000 cases in KZN , the second wave, came 6 months later and the province topped the charts with nearly 77 000 active cases. The highest in the whole country.

But the infection rate is already surging in Gauteng.

https://www.dut.ac.za/covid-19-statistics/

Up Sound
“And I look at how the epidemic is flowing in the first wave.”

V/O
Prof Salim Abdool Karim is a clinical infectious diseases epidemiologist who is the co-chair of the COVID ministerial advisory committee.


“In KZN the epidemic is spreading at a very rapid rate. That leads to a situation where the health care services are in a dire position. The number of cases are coming in rapidly, the patients are coming in needing hospital care all at the same time.”


V/O
This following video which went viral was filmed on the 4th of January.


Up Sound
“We are here at RK Khan outside as you can see, as you can see we are only seeing mortuary vans, plenty plenty of mortuary vans. I think there more vans than cars here, people are struggling to get in and out here, this pandemic is real.”

Link
We saw the second wave happen in other parts of the world, so we knew our turn coming. But little did we know that it would be accompanied by a dangerous new variant.

V/O
So how did we get here?
Prof Karim and scientists in South Africa have been studying this virus diligently.

Karim
“Over the first 7/8 months this virus hardly changed it was quite striking actually. This virus doesn’t change much, one or two mutations at most, didn’t bother us. I was lulled into a sense that this virus is stable and it is not mutating. We did not anticipate the come October there would be so mutations in one month. That’s game changer in terms of our response.”

V/O
Coupled with the fact that people had become tired of masking up and social distancing, one variant found the gap and literally spread like wildfire and is called 501Y.V2

Karim
“In the mix you now bring in a variant that is able to spread more efficiently and that variant is given opportunity to spread efficiently, with these super spreader events like the matric rage.”

V/O
Close to a thousand Gauteng matrics who went to Rage in Ballito were infected. And the variant literally went viral.

https://www.timeslive.co.za/news/south-africa/2020-12-13-984-pupils-from-gauteng-who-went-to-matric-rage-in-kzn-test-positive-for-covid-19/
www.worldometers.info


Moosa
“When I saw my first few patients in the second wave say about 5 or 6 weeks ago now, I immediately knew in the first week is that there is something different. What I noticed is that when you had an infection in the family, one member would be infected but now you have entire families have been infected.”

V/O
Dr Ashraff Moosa is a specialist physician.

Moosa
“It’s like a war zone, we are seeing numbers we never imagined we would see.

Up Sound
“A Second wave of COVID infections has been worst than expected hospitals are filling up…”

V/O
Sibongile Mzobe has seen households wiped out by COVID in Inanda. Her family has shut them selves off from the outside world to save their lives.

Masa
“How many funerals are you seeing in your area, how often.”

Sibongile
“Hey,hey, sometimes it can be a funeral today, may after tomorrow another funeral, that was on Saturday, funeral, funeral, funeral.”

V/O
Death literally came to her doorstep a month ago.




S’bo
I just get more scared after my neighbour just died. I was taking to her and then the next day gone. People are dying, dying like ants, you know.”

V/O
Dr Alex Sigal works at the Africa Health Research Intitute and showed us how powerful the SARS-COV-2 virus is at destroying cells as seen through a microscope.

Alex
“So for people who don’t think this virus is serious, what you are seeing here is cells that are not infected, they are motile which means they are moving around and talk to each other and mostly grow.”

V/O
This slide shows the effects on cells when they are infected with the virus.

Alex
“At the beginning everything is fine so it takes some time for the virus to actually get going but then what you are seeing is when these cells talk to each other, they start to fuse and the virus is transmitting from cell to cell and then after there is enough virus around these cells die.

Alex
“This is a serious cytotoxic virus.It affects in smart ways”

V/O
Scientists are warning that it is an ever changing scenario and SARS-COV-2 may still continue to mutate into more variants in the future.

Grave Diggers up sound
“As I have visited here 7 graves have been dug and anticipating the next burials they will take in next few hours.”

V/O
Dr Kevi Naidu runs a private practise and says that the virus shows no signs of slowing down in Durban yet.

Masa
“Are you patients able to accesss the medical care that they need?”

“So that has been a challenge, there isn’t a central mechanism for is to know as a primary care doctor in the field where the hospital beds are available, so I often have to call 6 or 7 hospital specialists on duty to before I can find a bed for a patient.”

V/O
Just after Christmas Valerie Potgieter’s partner Grahame Basson was critically ill with covid, there were no beds in Durban and he was sent 300km away to a hospital in Harrismith.

Valerie
“I am aware that there was a crisis brewing but I didn’t realise that it was so bad until we actually got to Westville ourselves . I think your automatic brain would say that if you went to the hospital you would be able to get a bed but there was none.”

V/O
Margie Christie couldn’t find a bed in Umhlanga and her brother who is a doctor saved her life at home.

Margie
“It’s very scary there, its very very full, many many people , there were some deaths that day.”

Paul
“Local hospitals are absolutely overwhelmed unfortunately the amount of patients infected supercede the amount of beds and capabilities available. So you have multiple patients outside lying on floors and lying on chairs, so the situation is currently in dire straights.

V/O
Paul Herbst is a paramedic in Ballito.

Paul
“The only way we currently are getting beds is not just from discharge but patients that are demysing in wards and hospitals.”

Kevi
“The issue being currently that there isn’t enough ICU and high care beds for everybody?”

Masa
“Is that for private and public hopsitals?”

Kevi
‘Yes it is for both.”

Masa
“So is the situation dire on either side, its doesn’t matter where you go?”

Kevi
“Correct”

Mansa
“You could have medical aid and you could still be in trouble.”

Kevi
“At this point it time, it is.”

V/O
These mortuary vans are waiting to pick up bodies at RK Khan Hospital , a visual image of the scale of the lives lost. South Africa knew the second wave would come, was it just bad planning?

Karim
“Back in August and September, the DOH and the WHO sent us ministerial a resurgence plan. So the planning for the second surge was planned well in advance. What we were not planning for was a variant that would spread like this.”

Kevi
“The unexpectedness of the spread that’s caused the challenge, so its burdened us ina way that no body could prepare for.”

Link
“It’s almost on a daily basis that when you log onto social media and you see medical staff post how they are fatigued and over worked and begging us to stay at home.”




V/O
And sadly COVID has taken the lives of hundreds of medical staff who were crucial in the fight on the front line.

Moosa
“This community of KwaZulu-Natal the general practitioners have really come to the party and I have lost 3 general practitioner friends simply because they are treating such a vast load of patients.

V/O
What everyone wants to know, is will the vaccine protect us against the new variant?

Karim
‘This is a key question. There is no evidence to suggest that vaccines don’t work against this variant or that they do. Fortunately the research is underway we can expect within the next week or two an announcement about each of different vaccines and if they are effective against 501YV2 variant.
So if people thought that in 2021 they could not wear maskas and stop our social distancing then I have bad news we are going to have to continue all of our prevention methods. A vaccine does not replace those, a cavvine is part and parcel of combination approach to controling this disease. At least until we can get heard immunity and even beyond that.


Promo 1
We anticipated a second COVID wave but we did not expect a more contagious variant. Infections are surging and medical facilities are battling to help the afflicted.

Promo 2
Hospitals are running out of beds, as the new, more contagious variant of SARS-COV -2 runs amok in KZN and Gauteng, resulting in much higher infections than of the first wave.

Promo 3
The health care system is buckling under the weight of the second COVID wave, made more contagious by 501YV2 variant. KZN and Gauteng are bearing the brunt of the storm.

Moosa “This community of KwaZulu-Natal the general practitioners have really come to the party and I have lost 3 general practitioner friends simply because they are treating such a vast load of patients. V/O What everyone wants to know, is will the vaccine protect us against the new variant? Karim ‘This is a key question. There is no evidence to suggest that vaccines don’t work against this variant or that they do. Fortunately the research is underway we can expect within the next week or two an announcement about each of different vaccines and if they are effective against 501YV2 variant. So if people thought that in 2021 they could not wear maskas and stop our social distancing then I have bad news we are going to have to continue all of our prevention methods. A vaccine does not replace those, a cavvine is part and parcel of combination approach to controling this disease. At least until we can get heard immunity and even beyond that. Promo 1 We anticipated a second COVID wave but we did not expect a more contagious variant. Infections are surging and medical facilities are battling to help the afflicted. Promo 2 Hospitals are running out of beds, as the new, more contagious variant of SARS-COV -2 runs amok in KZN and Gauteng, resulting in much higher infections than of the first wave. Promo 3 The health care system is buckling under the weight of the second COVID wave, made more contagious by 501YV2 variant. KZN and Gauteng are bearing the brunt of the storm.

metadata.Further information: KZN has become the epicentre of the COVID crisis at the moment. People are unable to get the medical attention that they need. Ambulances are turned away from hopsitals. The system just cannot cope. In early December it was projected that the surge would move from the Eastern and Western Cape to Kwa-Zulu Natal. At the beginning of December we saw a spike in cases because matrics attended RAGE. Over 1000 young aduls were affected and they took that back to where they originally came from. KZN then had the influx of holiday makers to our shores. With the added complication of mask fatigue it was just a powder keg waiting to explode. Yesterday Umhlanga hospital ran out of oxygen. It is not the fault of the hopsitals that they cannot cope. It is a problem worlwide of countries not being able to cope with the volume of patients. Lack of staff over stretched personel sub optimal health care. 8723 health care workers infected with COVID since beginning of the pandemic. 98 have died (1%) and 56% of those were nurses. Video footage of guard of honour Umhlanga hospital 18 deaths in past two days. Second wave worse than first. Prince Msheiyeni Hospital in Umlazi CEO told families that mortuary has reached its capacity. Some state hospitals like Prince Mshiyeni not able to sparate COVID with non COVID. Shortage of coffins. Mluleki Madlala of Madlala Funeral Services. He says body count triple as opposed to other Decembers. Increase of aout 10 bodies a day at crematorium. Extend burning till 11pm at night. Dr Richard Lessells of KRISP will talk about the new variant, how it developed and what the new charactersics are. It seems that it is more contagious and affects a wider range of people. Prof Karim will grant us an interview on Monday. (Before he sees the BBC) Dr Alex Signal works at the Africal Health Research Insititute and he has been testing the difference between the two variuants. Apparently they are on the brink of some new information about the virus which they will release in a week. I am hoping we can break this on Carte Blanche I will be seaking to him this morning. Michelle heads up a private Ambulance service called Meditech and they are allowing a cameraman to go with them on their rounds. She talks very clearly about patients being turned away. Dr Kevi Naidu is a gem and he has a practise in Berea. He looks after the Salvation Army Old Age home across the way from him. There are 50 people in the old age home. 26 have covid and two have died. They cannot get to hopsital because of their age and they rely on donations from people for medicine. They have all been quarentined in their little rooms and there is nothing they can do but see how the virus plays out . It is a real waiting game. We cannot interview any of them but there is some footage on Facebook and we can talk to their leader in Johannesburg. Dr Ashraf Moosa is part of a private hospital consortium and will give the perspective of the hopsitals. He is on various medical boards and speak very authoratively on what is happening. Patients. Anele Mzobe lives in Eastern Cape, went home for holidays, knew people had attended a funeral many were infected and died because it is just too far to get to a hospital. He lives in a settlement called Frasier and works in Ballito. He says he has seen many people dying there too. Owen Govender, son of Vanessa Govender who died working on COVID wards. RK Khan Hopsital. Gave her a guard of honour. Left a message for journalist to get their contact numbers. 0740657007 Valeria Jordan Graham on oxygen machine , got pneumonia. 61 turns on 23rd. Go to hospital get medical attention. Just continue panado. 23rd of December on birthday, fevers, Christmas better and not great. Fevers never broke, Valerie got sick on 26th, Monday got tests Tues, none get better get worse. Westville hopsital say, Admitted us lay in tent, put onto drips, afternoon blood results high and had pneumonia, very hot, did not know what happened. Found beds in Harrismith. Graham sent Harrismith, 5 or 6 to Harrismith. Tues 1st of January. In hospital since 29th. Ambulance in hot car. Relieved go home, couldn’t treat him at home. Stubborn person. It’s been horrible. Hasn’t heard from him. Can’t speak because of oxygen. Send he is OK. Staff is hectic, very full, limited insulin, running haggard.
